articles.title: RBI raises share of domestically held gold reserves, data shows
articles.desc: As of September, the Reserve Bank of India has expanded its domestic gold reserves to 880.52 metric tonnes. This figure comprises 740.13 metric tonnes held in the country and 140.39 metric tonnes stored internationally. However, the proportion of gold within the overall reserves has declined to 14.38%. Currently, India's total foreign exchange reserves stand at $705.3 billion, predominantly invested in foreign government securities.

Regulatory ambiguity poses a significant hurdle, with 59 percent expressing concerns. Investors frequently turn to informal channels, such as peer networks and social media, for insights on digital assets.

articles.desc: The Reserve Bank of India recorded net purchases of $6.94 billion in the foreign exchange market during September. It bought a total of $82.18 billion while selling $75.25 billion in currency transactions. Despite a decline in the rupee, capital inflows reached about $143 billion due to various measures. Indian equities have recently attracted investors, leading to a rise in the rupee's value.

SEBI eases KYC norms, centralises supplementary client data to simplify onboarding
articles.desc: SEBI has revealed new measures aimed at simplifying the client onboarding process for investors. By centralising supplementary KYC details with KYC Registration Agencies, investors can avoid repetition. The revised framework will take effect on December 24, 2026, enhancing efficiency in data management. Intermediaries are instructed to report account closures promptly to maintain accurate KYC records. Investors are also advised against engaging with grey market premium figures for IPOs.

articles.title: Sebi mulls early payout of up to 80% of sale proceeds to FPOs in commodity derivatives market
articles.desc: Sebi introduced a proposal for an early pay-out framework designed to assist Farmer Producer Organisations. This framework would allow FPOs to access up to 80 percent of sale proceeds before contract expiry. The initiative aims to alleviate liquidity challenges by providing timely payments to farmers. Corporate trading members will offer this facility based on certain conditions and net worth requirements. Public comments on the proposal are invited until December 16.

articles.title: RBI may opt for 25 bps rate hike as oil eases, inflation risks persist: Baroda BNP Paribas MF CIO
articles.desc: The Reserve Bank of India is projected to implement a 0.25 percent interest rate hike in December. While decreasing crude oil prices could alleviate some inflation worries, many senior executives advocate for a measured strategy due to the prevailing economic climate. Nevertheless, concerns regarding food inflation and supply chain issues persist, adversely influencing overall forecasts.

articles.title: US Treasury gains lift India bonds ahead of RBI meet
articles.desc: On Wednesday, Indian government bonds rallied, influenced by a decrease in US Treasury yields. The benchmark 10-year bond yield fell to 7.1641%, marking a two-week low. The Indian rupee strengthened to its highest level for the fiscal year against the dollar. Overseas investors returned as net buyers of Indian debt, purchasing over 93 billion rupees. The Reserve Bank of India's upcoming decision will significantly affect market movements and trends.

articles.desc: US inflation is expected to increase again in October, with potential implications for Federal Reserve interest rate decisions. Economists predict the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index to reach 3.8% this month. Analysts are divided regarding whether inflation is caused by demand or supply shocks stemming from recent policies. Market forecasts suggest three more rate hikes, signaling ongoing concerns about rising prices.

articles.desc: PhonePe has resumed its initial public offering plans after deferring them due to market uncertainties. The company aims for a stock market listing valued between USD 12-15 billion in early 2024. It expects to raise approximately Rs 12,000-14,000 crore through an offer-for-sale. The digital payments firm has also reported significant revenue growth and is now profitable at the group level.

articles.title: India's sugar output seen falling to decade low, says industry body
articles.desc: India's sugar production is expected to fall to a decade low of 26.52 million metric tons in the 2026/27 season, down from 27.97 million tons a year earlier, as lower rainfall is likely to hurt sugar cane yields in key growing states, the Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association said.

articles.title: Rupee scales 8-month high after holiday as foreign flows to Indian equities persist
articles.desc: The Indian rupee has shown significant strength against the US dollar, propelled by robust foreign portfolio investments. Surging to an eight-month high on Thursday, it closed at 92.23 per dollar. Analysts connect this to favorable market dynamics, including falling crude oil prices. With record foreign investments in Indian stocks this month, the market exudes increased confidence, suggesting a potential for continued rupee appreciation if circumstances remain favorable.

articles.desc: Indian businesses are preparing to increasingly deploy artificial intelligence agents across their operations, with 93 per cent of leaders intending to use the technology to expand workforce capabilities and 59 per cent already using AI agents to automate workstreams or business processes, according to a joint report by KPMG in India and the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII).

articles.title: AI fails to deliver significant earnings gains for most banks despite productivity boost: McKinsey
articles.desc: Banks are yet to convert widespread productivity gains from artificial intelligence (AI) into significant financial returns, with only 6 per cent of surveyed organisations attributing a substantial share of their earnings to the technology, highlighting the need to redesign business processes rather than simply introduce AI tools, according to a McKinsey report.

articles.title: HPE shares crash 17%, stock suffers its worst-ever single-day fall. Here's why
articles.desc: Hewlett Packard Enterprise shares plunged 17.1%, their steepest single-day fall since 2015, despite record quarterly revenue and stronger FY2027 guidance. Concerns over shrinking margins, rising component costs and supply constraints triggered the selloff.
